opportunities.title: Fix the leasing front door and make availability answerable and bookable by AI assistants
opportunities.problem: The prospect path is phone-gated and mobile-broken at the same time: the pricing page lists a dozen buildings with per-unit rents but headlines 'CALL FOR DETAILS' under 'Now Leasing for the Spring Semester', the contact form has four fields and no phone number, there is no online application or tour booking anywhere, and at a 390px viewport the page still lays out 768px wide so navigation and form fields are clipped off-screen. The site also gives a machine nothing to read (JSON-LD is a bare WebSite node with no LocalBusiness/address/hours) and hides 100+ reviews because the Google/Birdeye listing is unclaimed and no review widget sits on the site.
evidence: Pricing page: ~a dozen buildings, rents $1,210-$4,200, most 'Available June 1, 2027', banner 'Now Leasing for the Spring Semester' and 'CALL FOR DETAILS' — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list
Contact page offers only first name, last name, email, message plus an office phone — no phone field, no unit-of-interest, no move-in date — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us
At a 390px viewport the document scrollWidth is 768 (CSS sets min-width 768px on the wrapper), so nav and form fields are clipped — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us
Office hours M-F 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, closed weekends; Google shows 'Closed - Opens 9 AM Mon' — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/location-map

Listing is unclaimed and shows 4.0 stars from 102 reviews (70 five-star vs 18 one-star); no review widget appears on the company site — https://reviews.birdeye.com/premier-properties-of-new-brunswick-rutgers-off-campus-housing-164556339877922

Site still shows '© 2022 All Rights Reserved' and the linked /management-services page is lorem ipsum, while content is updated for 2026-2027 availability — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/management-services
Floor plans are published as JPG images, so prices, square footage and unit numbers are not structured data — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/property/191-hamilton-street
opportunities.agent_design: Agent-built front door on the existing Duda site plus a thin service layer: (1) responsive rebuild of the home, pricing, building, FAQ and contact templates with a real headline above the fold and a per-building 'check availability / request a tour' funnel that captures phone, unit type, move-in date and budget; (2) LocalBusiness + ApartmentComplex JSON-LD with address, hours and per-building price ranges, emitted from the same structured unit feed the agent uses; (3) an availability answering agent on web chat and the form that answers price, move-in date, utilities, pet, laundry and tour-policy questions from the published text and the AppFolio unit state, then either books an open-house slot or opens a qualification call; (4) a human always confirms any tour outside the seasonal open houses, because the company's stated policy is office qualification first; (5) claim the Google/Birdeye listing and pull reviews onto the site. Triggers: form submit, chat message, availability query that cannot be answered from the feed. Systems touched: Duda site, AppFolio unit/lease data (read), Google Business Profile. Escalation: anything touching deposits, the Preferred Tenants List or a rent exception goes to the general manager's inbox.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A site-builder template cannot emit consistent LocalBusiness/ApartmentComplex structured data or keep published prices truthful against AppFolio unit state, and a chatbot subscription cannot answer 'is a 2-bed at 15 Union free June 1' without a feed. This is a two-way integration plus schema work plus a listing claim, with a policy constraint (office qualification before tours) that has to be encoded rather than removed.

impact_estimate.range: Customer-visible fix today: a phone search that currently renders 768px wide on a 390px screen becomes usable, and 'CALL FOR DETAILS' becomes an answerable, bookable path. Conservative financial range: 0 to +4.8% scheduled visits on the traffic that reaches the new booking path, i.e. an order of 5-15 additional scheduled tours per leasing wave at today's volume; each additional signed 12-month lease is worth $14,520-$50,400 in annual rent (published rent range $1,210-$4,200/mo).
impact_estimate.assumptions: Rent range taken from the company's own per-unit pricing (not an estimate). The +4.8% scheduled-visit lift is from a single production A/B result on a large rental marketplace (arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed) and is applied as an upper bound, not a forecast. Assumes no analytics baseline exists today (none is published) so the first month is measurement; assumes tours convert to leases at a rate that is unknown and not asserted here. Does not count the CTA/structured-data gain for AI-assistant referrals, which cannot be quantified without traffic data.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: responsive rebuild of five templates with an above-fold offer; JSON-LD on home/pricing/building pages; one integrated availability + tour-request funnel (phone, unit type, move-in date) writing to AppFolio and email; Google listing claimed and 3 recent reviews surfaced; before/after numbers on mobile scrollWidth, mobile bounce and enquiries captured after hours.

opportunities.title: After-hours prospect intake and follow-up agent for the two annual re-leasing waves
opportunities.problem: The buyer is a Rutgers student or an out-of-state parent searching evenings and weekends, while the office is open M-F 9-5 and closed both weekend days. Every price and availability question is deliberately routed to a phone call, the only written path captures no phone number (so a call-back needs an email round trip), and one $22/hr Leasing Assistant posting bundles prospect calls, applications, credit reports, tours, inspections, work orders and deposit collection into a single seat. Because most of ~350 units run 12-month leases starting June 1 or September 1, nearly the whole portfolio re-leases in two waves that land on finals and graduations — the posting even requires Memorial Day weekend availability.
evidence: Leasing Assistant, $22/hr, full-time onsite Mon-Fri, posted Sep 24 2026 / updated Oct 27 2026 and now expired; duties bundle incoming prospect calls, applications/credit reports/renewals, tours, inspections and turnovers, maintenance work orders, and security-deposit and rent collection — https://tallo.com/talent/job/hospitality/concierge/nj/new-brunswick/leasing-assistant-1-year-ex-8216cd26
Hours M-F 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, office closed Saturday and Sunday; single downtown office at 205 Easton Ave — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/location-map
Contact form has no phone field and no unit-of-interest or move-in date — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us
'CALL FOR DETAILS' on a page of per-unit prices means every availability question becomes a staff call — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list
12-month leases with most starting June 1 or September 1, so nearly the portfolio turns over in two waves — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us
No online application or tour scheduler exists; tours are open-house-only except for immediately available units — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/faq
opportunities.agent_design: An intake agent on three channels — missed-call/after-hours text-back, web chat, and inbound email to generalmanager@premiernb.com. It greets, asks for unit type, move-in date, budget, school/parent status and a callable number, answers from the published pricing and FAQ text (utilities excluded and PSE&G in tenant's name, flat water charge by building, no pets, 12-month term, tour policy), proposes either a seasonal open-house slot or a qualification call, writes a structured lead into AppFolio/CRM with the transcript, and sends one follow-up if the prospect goes quiet. Human approval gates: any tour outside open houses, any price or deposit exception, anything involving the Preferred Tenants List, out-of-state or foreign applicants, or credit/adverse-action language — those are handed to the leasing assistant or GM. Compliance: prefer text and email with explicit opt-in for outbound; if an AI voice agent makes calls, follow the FCC's AI-call disclosure/consent proceeding (89 FR 73321) and keep a human in the loop on anything that sounds like a commitment.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It has to hold multi-channel state, write back into AppFolio so a lead is not lost when the leasing assistant opens the file the next morning, answer from live per-unit availability rather than a static script, and enforce an escalation policy and audit trail. A website chatbot widget cannot do the write-back, the follow-up cadence or the consent handling.

impact_estimate.range: About 2-5 staff hours/week off-season and 8-15 hours/week during the May-June and August-September waves returned to leasing and admin work, i.e. roughly $350-$1,300/month of capacity at peak and $4k-$16k/year gross at the posted $22/hr; plus same-evening response to enquiries that today wait until Monday.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Wage taken directly from the company's own expired Leasing Assistant posting ($22/hr). Volumes are not published, so hours are inferred from a 350-unit portfolio re-leasing in two waves against a one-seat leasing desk; assumes 30-40% of first-contact handling time is automatable, extrapolated from a customer-support study (NBER working paper — a working paper, not peer-reviewed — reporting a 14% average gain in issues resolved per hour, larger for novices) rather than from any property-management measurement, because none exists. Excludes any revenue effect from faster response, which is real but unsourced here. Constrained by the company's deliberate office-qualification policy: the agent does not replace qualification, it captures and pre-qualifies.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: missed-call text-back plus email/form triage plus a published-answer chat on one building cluster (Easton Ave/Union St), with escalation rules and wording signed off by the general manager, a weekly transcript review to catch wrong answers, and a report of after-hours enquiries captured, median time-to-first-response and tours booked.

opportunities.title: AppFolio-connected leasing pipeline: one availability source of truth plus application and Preferred-Tenants packet intake
opportunities.problem: AppFolio already holds the units, leases, payments and work orders, but the public availability list is hand-maintained text on a static page showing '© 2022', the guessed /availability-and-pricing URL 404s while /pricing-list works, floor plans exist only as JPGs, and there is no online application or tour scheduler at all. On the back end, each prospect is walked manually through an application, a W-9, a Preferred Tenant Agreement, a $500 refundable deposit and electronic lease signing — including a program for out-of-state and foreign renters who cannot come to the office — and only a completed lease holds a unit. With Union Square's 150 approved units adding roughly 40% more doors, that per-prospect paperwork load scales with units, not with headcount.
evidence: Site footer carries 'Powered by AppFolio Property Manager'; residents pay rent and submit maintenance requests through the AppFolio portal, so the system of record already exists — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/location-map
Availability is a single hand-maintained text page with per-unit prices and move-in dates, no structured data, and a 2022 copyright — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list

Application process: applying does not hold a unit, only a completed lease guarantees a spot; Preferred Tenants List requires an application, W-9, Preferred Tenant Agreement and $500 refundable deposit — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us
No online application or tour booking exists; the only conversion paths are phone, mailto and a four-field form — https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us

Leasing Assistant duties include processing lease applications, credit reports and renewals and collecting security deposits and rent from new residents — https://tallo.com/talent/job/hospitality/concierge/nj/new-brunswick/leasing-assistant-1-year-ex-8216cd26
150-unit, $60M Union Square at 40/46/50 Union St approved; a Construction Management Associates / Premier Properties subsidiary — https://jerseydigs.com/union-square-new-brunswick/
opportunities.agent_design: An agent-built internal tool plus two integrations. (1) Nightly read-only pull from AppFolio (unit, rent, availability date, lease status) into a structured availability feed that drives the website, the JSON-LD block and the chat/voice agents — so a price is never published from a hand-typed page. (2) Application intake: prospect starts an application online, uploads application/W-9/ID/pay stubs, and a document-extraction agent returns structured fields, flags missing items, and drafts the Preferred Tenant Agreement packet, deposit instructions and lease-signing invite for the GM to approve and send. (3) A leasing dashboard by wave (June 1 vs September 1) with pipeline stage, stalled-prospect and signing-deadline alerts. Humans approve every approval/denial and every document sent; tenant screening stays in the existing consumer-reporting flow so FCRA permissible-purpose, disclosure/authorization and adverse-action duties are preserved, and applicant PII stays in a role-restricted store with audit logging.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It needs AppFolio API/report access, idempotent two-way sync so the published list cannot drift, structured extraction from scanned and checkbox-heavy documents, PII access control and audit logging for applicant files. A form builder plus a spreadsheet cannot keep 350+ published prices truthful or handle multi-document packets reliably, and a wrong published price is a fair-housing-adjacent misrepresentation risk, not just an ops bug.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 20-50 staff hours returned per leasing wave (1-3 hrs/week of availability-list upkeep plus 15-30 minutes of manual entry per application on an assumed 40-120 applications per wave), i.e. about $440-$1,100 per wave at the posted $22/hr; the larger, unquantified gain is eliminating stale published pricing and mis-set prospect expectations before a call.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Wage from the company's own Leasing Assistant posting ($22/hr); application counts are not published and are inferred from ~350 units re-leasing in two waves. Document-extraction reliability is assumed at the level reported by an arXiv preprint (35 structured attributes from 3,965 property questionnaire documents, 0.82 Jaccard consistency; preprint, not peer-reviewed) — the pilot must measure accuracy on the company's own packets before any volume commitment. Union Square's 150 units are approved but construction was described as years out, so no impact is attributed to them.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: read-only AppFolio availability export turned into one structured feed driving a single building cluster's pages; an online application start plus document-intake agent run on 10 real packets with human review on every one; measured minutes-per-packet and error rate against today's manual process; dashboard mock for one leasing wave.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (25/30): unusually well-evidenced rather than inferred — a measured 768px layout on a 390px screen, a phone-gated pricing page, a four-field form with no phone number, an expired $22/hr job posting that bundles the whole leasing desk into one seat, and a review profile split 70 five-star vs 18 one-star. Missing the last few points only because individual review text could not be read and no enquiry volume or analytics baseline is published. Fit (18/20): three of the consultancy's lanes land almost exactly on the firm's structure — G on a front door triage measured page by page, A on a one-seat leasing desk with two annual surges, D on AppFolio data that exists but is not published. Strategic (13/15): a college-town, student-rental, AppFolio shop with a phone-gated leasing page is a highly repeatable template across Rutgers-adjacent and other campus markets. Ability to pay (15/20): ~350 managed units at $1,210-$4,200/month plus an approved 150-unit Union Square, so one additional lease covers most of a pilot; but it is an owner-operated shop with a single decision maker (Mitch Broder) and no published revenue, and its pattern is to hire one $22/hr generalist rather than buy software. Ease (11/15): the site is a small Duda build and AppFolio is standard, but the phone-first, office-qualification tour policy is deliberate and must be encoded rather than removed, and live AppFolio write access will need the GM's cooperation. Why not a physical/edge (E) opportunity: no avenues.json evidence pack was supplied for this task, and the profile's physical signals show cameras and access control already installed and serviced (24/7 video surveillance, electronic entrance locking), with no observed pain in temperature, equipment, inventory or counting to build on — so an E pitch here would rest on speculation plus NJ alarm-business licensing overhead (N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2, as amended by P.L.2021, c.2) for no evidenced gain. Revisit E only if a walkthrough surfaces a real operations problem (laundry-room equipment, package-room overflow at 191 Hamilton, mechanical-room leaks).

best_evidence_signal: The pricing page lists a dozen buildings with per-unit rents of $1,210-$4,200 under 'Now Leasing for the Spring Semester' and the headline 'CALL FOR DETAILS' — availability is deliberately phone-gated in a market whose buyers are students and out-of-state parents shopping at night and on weekends: https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list
suggested_channel: walk-in at 205 Easton Ave (M-F 9-5, ask for the general manager), then a short email to generalmanager@premiernb.com; no careers page or named GM is published, so the office is the reliable route and Mitch Broder is the named president
